rules.text: If the query image shows a drastic change in time of day (e.g., bright daylight) compared to the reference images (e.g., night), trust A (Agent) to correctly identify this as a normal contextual variation rather than an anomaly.

If the query image contains large, semi-transparent, or geometrically perfect rectangular artifacts (e.g., green blocks, light projections) that appear to be camera sensor noise or lens flares rather than physical road objects, trust B (Direct) to classify the scene as normal.

If the query image contains bright, diffuse lighting artifacts (e.g., sun glare, lens flare) that obscure parts of the scene but do not represent physical obstacles on the road, trust B (Direct) to classify the scene as normal.
The camera viewpoint is from inside a vehicle, with the dashboard or hood visible at the bottom of the frame.
The drivable road surface occupies the central and lower portion of the image, extending into the distance.
Ignore dark, elongated shadows or debris-like shapes on the road surface if they are consistent with low-light conditions or road texture.
Do not flag pedestrians standing on sidewalks or near curbs as road obstacles unless they are clearly stepping into the active driving lane.
Treat bright reflections, billboards, or light bars on vehicles as normal environmental features rather than defects or anomalies.
